extracted.intended_audience: writers and production staff at WGA-signatory companies (participating writers, company reps, Credits/Contracts staff)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules for preparing and submitting Notices of Tentative Writing Credits (NTWCs), documenting literary material, handling team-writing, requesting waivers, and assembling materials for credit arbitrations for theatrical motion pictures under the WGA MBA/TSA/SCM.

rubrics_metrics.name: NTWC submission timing and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: The NTWC must be submitted to the Guild and to all participating writers as soon as practicable following completion of principal photography. It sets in motion determination of credits, notifies writers of proposed credits and protest deadlines, and allows the Guild to determine whether automatic arbitration provisions are triggered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit immediately after principal photography; NTWC is critical for Company, writers, and the Guild to finalize credits in timely fashion. See TSA, ¶11 and SCM pp. 4–6.

rubrics_metrics.name: List all participating writers on NTWC
rubrics_metrics.description: List the names and addresses of all participating writers at the top of the NTWC. You must list the names of all participating writers, even if they are not proposed for credit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A “participating writer” includes anyone who participated in screenplay writing, was employed on story/screenplay, or a professional writer who sold/licensed literary material subject to the MBA (see Article 1.B.1.b.). If unsure who should be listed, contact the Guild for a Participating Writer Investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted methods of delivering the NTWC
rubrics_metrics.description: The NTWC must be sent via Certified Mail/Return Receipt Requested, messenger, or other independently verifiable means. Email delivery to the writer is allowed only with specific contract provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Email only if (a) writer expressly agreed to receive notices by email in personal services contract, (b) writer’s email address is provided, and (c) the writer’s designated personal representative’s individual email address is also provided; the representative must also receive notice. (TSA, ¶¶2.d., 12, 17.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Include motion picture title on NTWC
rubrics_metrics.description: The NTWC must list the title of the motion picture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the title is accurately entered in the specified NTWC field (Form item B).

rubrics_metrics.name: List production executives and disclose dual roles
rubrics_metrics.description: List the names of all production executives (director, producers, executive/co/associate producers, etc.). If a participating writer is also proposed to be credited as a production executive, that must be indicated on the NTWC and notice given before writing credits are determined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to indicate dual-credit situations can trigger issues; notify all parties when a participating writer will also be credited as a production executive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed on-screen writing credit (form matters)
rubrics_metrics.description: List the proposed on-screen writing credit including the form of credit (e.g., “Written by”, “Screenplay by”, etc.), not just the writer name(s). Writers may only be credited in the manner set forth in the MBA unless a waiver is granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowable forms include “Written by,” “Screenplay by,” “Story by,” “Screen Story by,” “Adaptation by,” “Narration Written by,” and “Based on Characters Created by.” Contact the Credits Department for questions. (TSA, ¶¶1–2; SCM pp. 13–14.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of ampersand vs 'and' and definition of team
rubrics_metrics.description: An ampersand (“&”) is used between the names of writers who worked as a team on the motion picture; the word “and” is used between names of writers who did not work as a team. A “team” is defined as two (or more) writers assigned at about the same time to the same material who work together for approximately the same length of time on the material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Writers who meet the services-based definition are considered a team for credits purposes even if they do not regularly write as a bona fide team. (SCM, pp. 3–4.) Note SCM also limits team size (no more than two writers, or three in some Article 13.A.9 situations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Include on-screen source material credit on NTWC
rubrics_metrics.description: Include any on-screen source material credit (e.g., “Based on the Novel by”) on the NTWC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'Novel' for fiction works and 'Book' for non-fiction generally. Ensure source-author names and form of source credit are accurate. (TSA, ¶2; SCM, pp. 2–3.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Include presentation/production credits on NTWC
rubrics_metrics.description: Include on the NTWC any presentation and/or production credit to be accorded on screen and/or in advertising (e.g., “Universal Pictures Presents” or “A Film by”).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List presentation/production credits in the specified NTWC field so these placements are considered when determining final credits. (TSA, ¶28.)

rubrics_metrics.name: List all source material regardless of screen appearance
rubrics_metrics.description: List any source material upon which the motion picture is based, regardless of whether it will appear on screen. This includes prior motion pictures in the case of a remake or sequel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure complete disclosure of source material so Guild can verify appropriate source credits and rights (Form item G).

rubrics_metrics.name: Send final shooting script to all participating writers
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy of the final shooting script must be sent to all participating writers, including those who are not proposed for credit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is required concurrently with NTWC distribution. (TSA, ¶11.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper calculation of final date / protest period
rubrics_metrics.description: Properly calculate and state the date on which the proposed credits become final absent a protest. Generally credits become final twelve business days from the date the NTWC is sent; this may shorten to seven business days if a good faith emergency exists and is requested on the NTWC. If automatic arbitration applies, write “Automatic Arbitration” in place of a final date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If NTWC is revised, recalculates the final date from the new dispatch date and deliver the revised NTWC to all participating writers. (TSA, ¶13.)

rubrics_metrics.name: NTWC must include company contact and signature
rubrics_metrics.description: List the name, address, and telephone number of the production company and authorized representative, and ensure the NTWC is signed by the authorized representative of the Company; include the date the NTWC is sent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The date on which the NTWC is actually sent (not prepared) is the operative dispatch date for deadlines. Use the proper signature and company information fields (Form items J, K).

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaboration Agreement requirement for certain teams
rubrics_metrics.description: A Collaboration Agreement is required when a production executive writes in collaboration as a team with a non-production executive writer where the production executive intends to claim co-authorship of the team’s material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A writing services agreement employing the production executive and the non-production executive as a team is a form of Collaboration Agreement. Contact Contracts Department for questions. (SCM, pp. 3–4.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Team waivers for large writing teams
rubrics_metrics.description: Team waivers are required for writing teams of four or more people (note SCM/TSA generally define a team as no more than two writers, or three in limited Article 13 circumstances).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Waivers must be requested and approved in advance of services being performed. Contact Contracts Department (phone/email provided) to request a team waiver. (TSA, ¶4; SCM pg. 3.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Arbitration triggers (protests and automatic arbitration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Generally a credit arbitration is triggered by the timely receipt of a protest by a participating writer or the Guild. Automatic arbitration is required in certain situations specified by the MBA/TSA/SCM.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Automatic arbitration circumstances include: (1) when a production executive is proposed for writing credit and there are other non-production executive participating writers; (2) when a “Screen Story by” credit is proposed; (3) when an “Adaptation by” credit is proposed; and (4) when three writers are proposed for “Written by” or “Screenplay by” credit (a team counts as a single writer). (TSA, ¶13; SCM, pp. 5, 13–18.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Materials required for arbitration submission
rubrics_metrics.description: In the case of an arbitration, the Company must submit three copies of all literary material submitted to or acquired by the Company by all participating writers and any source material, and a transmittal letter identifying each piece of literary material by author and date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Literary material includes beat sheets, outlines, stories, treatments, scripts, formats, etc. Source material includes previously exploited material and material not written under Guild jurisdiction. Submit these as soon as possible upon receipt of a protest or concurrently with NTWC in automatic arbitration. (TSA, ¶18.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover page requirements on literary material (Article 37 compliance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cover pages on all literary material must comply with MBA Article 37: upon commencement of pre-production, Company shall place the name of the initial writer on literary material followed by the word “revisions” preceding the names of subsequent writers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The cover page must show the first writer followed by 'revisions' and indicate contributions of subsequent writers via 'current revisions by' with the writer’s name and submission date. Proper format alleviates disputes in arbitration; samples are attached in the Guide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover pages track, do not adjudicate, authorship/credit
rubrics_metrics.description: The cover page is NOT a statement of authorship of the project or an assessment of writing credit; it is a means of tracking who the writers on a project are and which writer is responsible for the changes in each draft.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not remove names of earlier writers from cover pages even if you believe none of their material remains. Accurately reflect prior writers and the writer responsible for changes in each document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waivers required for certain screenings and combined credits
rubrics_metrics.description: Waivers from the Guild are required for (1) writing teams of four or more; (2) screenings in advance of the Guild’s final determination of writing credits (e.g., film festivals / public exhibitions); and (3) combining certain credits (e.g., 'Written, Produced, and Directed by'; 'Written and Produced by'; 'Written for the Screen and Directed by'; 'Written by' when same writer entitled to both 'Screen Story by' and 'Screenplay by').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact the appropriate Guild department (Contracts or Credits) to request required waivers well in advance. (TSA, ¶4, ¶26 and SCM cross-references.)

rubrics_metrics.name: On-screen placement of writing credits
rubrics_metrics.description: Writing credits generally must appear on a separate card contiguous to the director’s credit. Placement rules for 'Screenplay by' and 'Story by' depend on main vs end titles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Main titles: if 'Screenplay by' and 'Story by' appear on same card, 'Screenplay by' must be in top 50% of card; if on separate cards, 'Story by' must precede 'Screenplay by'. End titles: 'Screenplay by' always precedes 'Story by' and may appear on same or separate cards. Writing credit must appear in main titles if any personal names (or portions) appear in main titles. (TSA, ¶8.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement rules for source material credits
rubrics_metrics.description: Source material credit may appear in the main or end titles and should be on a separate card from the writing credit, except when the source material author is also the sole credited writer of the screenplay (then it may appear on same card).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The source material credit may not be placed between the 'Screenplay by' credit and the director’s credit when credits are on separate cards. Review TSA ¶¶2.d, 8, 22, 27 and 28 and the SCM for full placement rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit main and end titles to WGA for approval
rubrics_metrics.description: You are required to submit the main and end titles for the picture to the WGA for approval before any prints are prepared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures on-screen credits conform to the MBA and helps avoid penalties for non-compliance. (TSA, ¶8.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit all advertising and publicity material to WGA for approval
rubrics_metrics.description: All publicity and advertising material must be submitted to the WGA for approval prior to issuance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compliance ensures publicity and advertising conform to MBA provisions and helps avoid penalties. Contact the Credits Department for submissions. (TSA, ¶26.)
